effort: Control backward momentum and choose a clean forward reversal or open-turn running exit.
brief: E2 is a backpedal-to-forward reversal with facing unchanged. A backward stop isolates braking, sprint-to-backpedal reverses the gait order, a backward landing checks absorption, a drop-step initiation opens a new path, and an open turn converts backward gait into running along the same travel line.
marker: For E2, record a controlled backward brake, no heel-crossing or backward fall, and two forward exit steps on the return line. Distinguish this reversal from E6's same-travel-direction open turn.
readiness: The athlete must backpedal comfortably at short distance and see the coach's setup before moving. Keep backward speed low enough to stop inside the marked zone; no blind pursuit or external surprise cue.
space: All travel can follow one 10 m lane, mirrored one direction at a time. Keep its entire length clear, including the backward stopping corridor; verify width and side clearance. E5's stationary opening is oriented so the resulting run stays down the lane.

drills.name: Backpedal-to-Stick
drills.execution: Backpedal 2 m, brake over 1.5 m and hold a balanced two-foot stance for 2 s.
drills.job: Isolate stopping backward travel before asking for another exit.
drills.layout: Face the 0 m end, start at 2, backpedal to 4 and stop by 5.5; keep the rest of the lane empty.
drills.difference: Backward gait and backward braking replace the forward/lateral terminal stops already used.
drills.regress: Shorten steps/speed if heels cross, torso leans back or vision leaves the coach.

drills.name: Backpedal-to-Forward Reversal
drills.execution: Face toward 10 m; backpedal 2 m, brake before the turn line and drive forward 2 m without turning the torso; stop over 3 m.
drills.job: Main reversal of backward momentum into a forward first step.
drills.layout: Start at 5 m, backpedal toward 3, reverse at 3, run to 5 and stop by 8. Keep 0–3 clear for an aborted reversal.
drills.difference: Travel reverses while facing stays constant; Class 1's running shuttle required a body turn.
drills.regress: Slow the backpedal if the final backward step reaches excessively or the restart needs a hop.

drills.name: Sprint-to-Backpedal Transition
drills.execution: Run forward 2 m, brake and backpedal 2 m along the return without spinning; stop within 1 m.
drills.job: Organize the legs to push backward after forward braking.
drills.layout: Start at 2 m, run to 4, backpedal to 2 and stop by 1; keep 4–7 clear for an aborted transition.
drills.difference: Forward-to-backward gait order contrasts with E2's backward-to-forward task and requires a different first exit action.
drills.regress: Reduce approach speed if the athlete turns instead of backpedaling or cannot stop within the return zone.
drills.exposure: 1 travel reversal, turn braking plus terminal stopping.

drills.name: Backward Two-Foot Jump to Stick
drills.execution: Make a small backward two-foot jump within 0.3 m and hold the two-foot landing for 2 s; keep eyes forward.
drills.job: Accept backward-directed force without allowing the torso to fall behind the feet.
drills.layout: Centre of the clear lane; inspect the landing space before starting.
drills.difference: Backward bilateral flight and absorption, absent from the earlier forward/lateral/turning landing tasks.
drills.regress: Shorten the flight if balance shifts behind the heels.

drills.name: Drop-Step Crossover Go
drills.execution: Make a small near-leg drop step to open the hips, then cross the far leg and accelerate 2 m; stop over 3 m.
drills.job: Create room for the hips to turn before applying running force into a rearward exit.
drills.layout: Set the initial stance oblique to the lane so the declared drop-step/crossover exit runs down its long axis. Start at 2, accelerate to 4, stop by 7.
drills.difference: A drop step precedes the crossover; Class 1 expressly used crossover first with no drop step.
drills.regress: Make the opening step smaller if the athlete twists on the support leg.
drills.exposure: 1 stationary initiation and terminal stop, not an incoming-momentum cut.

drills.name: Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn — open, same travel heading
drills.execution: Backpedal 2 m, slow and open the hips through a half turn, then run another 2 m in the same direction of travel; stop over 2 m.
drills.job: Convert a backward gait into a stronger running exit without falsely treating the body turn as a travel reversal.
drills.layout: Start at 3 m facing 0, backpedal to 5, open to face 10, run to 7 and stop by 9. Keep metre 9–10 clear.
drills.difference: Facing changes while travel continues; E2 changes travel while facing stays fixed.
drills.regress: Reduce backpedal speed if feet tangle or the turn pivots on a locked knee.
drills.exposure: 0 travel-direction changes; 1 gait-transition braking phase and 1 final stop.

light.job: Keep the front knee and pelvis controlled as backward steps load the front leg.
Maintain a stable foot base when braking from a backward gait.

strength.job: Load the front leg while a controlled backward step changes the base, then drive back forward.
Support forceful hip extension through the forward restart after a backward stop.
Maintain frontal control for the open-turn and drop-step exits.
Retain knee-flexor heel-dig support for braking.
Adductor support controls pelvis height as the hips open.
Supply plantarflexion force as the forward exit lengthens from the low braking stance.

previous_review: Class 5 prescribed ten locomotor attempts, eight mixed running/flight-to-run redirections and six flight landings; no actual completion is reported.
progression: Change gait demands while keeping entries at 2 m and all exits short. Only six true travel reversals are prescribed; body turns are not counted as extra cuts. New backward skill does not justify maximal speed.
strength_progression: Keep lateral lunge, bridge and Copenhagen at their existing single-round doses. Introduce one round each of reverse lunge, hip thrust and supported standing calf work for backward-step loading and forward extension; calibrate loads with the listed ramps, not assumed prior ability.
audit: Separated backward reversal from same-heading open-turn mechanics and counted them differently. Omitted a longer backward course and reduced new lift working rounds to avoid combining novelty with volume escalation.
next: Next class introduces an obtuse running cut and crossover braking; inspect actual backward and lateral control plus recent load first.

light_entries.name: Lateral Step-Down — low support, light
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight first; a light dumbbell only if still easy. Lower **3 s**, lightly touch the free heel, return under control. Rest **30 s between legs; 45 s before S2**.
light_entries.regress: Rehearse the plant leg controlling knee travel and pelvic position during weight acceptance. Use the lowest stable support that permits a level pelvis and whole stance-foot contact; use hand support if needed. Reduce step height/load for knee collapse or pelvic drop.
light_entries.alternative: If the step is unsuitable, use instead a hand-supported shallow single-leg squat, the same 1 × 4 per leg and easy effort.
light_entries.job: Keep the front knee and pelvis controlled as backward steps load the front leg.

light_entries.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported standing hold
light_entries.execution: **5 s relaxed reset** between holds, **30 s between feet**, **60 s before P1**. Stand with most weight on the working foot and fingertip support.
light_entries.regress: Strengthen active arch control while maintaining heel, big-toe base and little-toe base contact for planting. Keep toes long; do not roll onto the outside edge. Use bilateral weight support instead if arch control needs toe-clawing or ankle rolling.
light_entries.job: Maintain a stable foot base when braking from a backward gait.

strength_entries.name: Reverse Lunge — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: Step backward under control, lower 2 s and drive through the original front foot to return. Keep knee tracking with the foot.
strength_entries.rest: Rest 60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce step length/load for an uncontrolled backward reach or front-heel lift.
strength_entries.job: Load the front leg while a controlled backward step changes the base, then drive back forward.

strength_entries.name: Hip Thrust — dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: Upper back on a stable bench, dumbbell secured over pelvis; rise to hip extension without arching the back, lower 2 s.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/range for lumbar extension or hamstring cramp.
strength_entries.alternative: If bench geometry is unsuitable, use instead a loaded dynamic floor glute bridge at the same rep/effort and preparation dose.
strength_entries.job: Support forceful hip extension through the forward restart after a backward stop.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Maintain frontal control for the open-turn and drop-step exits.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Retain knee-flexor heel-dig support for braking.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Adductor support controls pelvis height as the hips open.

strength_entries.name: Standing Calf Raise — supported dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: Nearly straight working knee, light hand support, 1 s at top and 2 s lowering to the floor.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load for bouncing or shortened heel rise.
strength_entries.job: Supply plantarflexion force as the forward exit lengthens from the low braking stance.
